text:
AI is burning Big Tech's free cash flow:

The combined CapEx of Amazon, $AMZN, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, and Microsoft, $MSFT, rose +$36.9 billion in Q3 2026, to a record $201.9 billion.

This figure has more than doubled over the last 12 months and is up +356% since Q1 2024.

Big Tech has now spent $1.6 trillion on CapEx over the last 3 years.

Meanwhile, the combined free cash flow of these companies fell -$33.1 billion last quarter, to -$26.4 billion, its lowest on record.

Free cash flow among these firms has dropped -$88.2 billion over the last year.

Only Microsoft reported positive free cash flow in Q3.

Looking ahead, these 4 companies plan to spend another $232 billion on CapEx in Q4, potentially lifting their combined CapEx to a record $740 billion in 2026.

Big Tech is undertaking one of the largest infrastructure buildouts in history.

The company generated its first quarterly operating profit. Revenue grew 1,368% YoY while compute expense rose only ~300%. Efficiency is rising, not collapsing.⁠

GPU rental prices have turned higher again. B200 on-demand rates rose more than 20% in a month in some indices; H100 and H200 also firmed. Tightness in the spot and short-term rental market is consistent with the hyperscalers’ own comments that they still cannot meet all the demand they see.⁠

text:
Gold’s 30% Drop Matches 2008, but a Bottom Is Near | Tavi Costa

Taken as one sector, #gold miners would have the cleanest balance sheets in the stock market, says Tavi Costa @TaviCosta , yet mining makes up less than 1% of it. The founder and CEO of Azuria Capital calls this pullback “one of the most compelling windows of opportunities” he has seen this cycle, and with gold down about 30% by his count, he thinks “we’re closer to the bottom.”

Speaking with Kitco News anchor Jeremy Szafron at the New Orleans Investment Conference, Costa points to free cash flow yields near 10% and bank models that still value the miners on $3,000 to $3,500 gold. Plug in a higher long-term price, he argues, and the whole industry gets re-rated. He is especially drawn to silver miners, some holding 10% to 15% of their market cap in cash, and he sees resources as the new moat in a world AI can disrupt, calling mining “the best AI trade.”
